method: Manuscript claims audited against the three dated/sourced research files (research/02_open_weights_multimodal.md, 03_open_tts_audio.md, 04_leaderboards_macro.md). Every substantive claim traces to a research item with a verifying URL. Window news vs. context flagged in research; manuscript uses anchored/relative dates and hedges all vendor/benchmark numbers ('they claim', 'trackers report', 'vendor blind test').
gate: PASS — no unresolved CORRECTED claims. TTS spend authorized.

must_fix_applied.correction: Changed display+audio to 'American models'. 'US' risked being read by the TTS voice as the word 'us'. Substance (US-origin models per OpenRouter telemetry) unchanged.

hedged_or_kept.claim: Best open models around 80% on SWE-bench Verified (Kimi K2.6, MiniMax; DeepSeek's biggest model claiming similar)
hedged_or_kept.note: Manuscript explicitly says 'claiming' and 'the trackers disagree with each other' and 'treat any single benchmark number as a claim, not a fact.' Trackers report ~80.2% (MiniMax M2.5, Kimi K2.6) and ~80.6% (DeepSeek V4 Pro Max, claimed); figures are unreconciled vendor/third-party mixes.

Manuscript says 'claims over 600 languages' and immediately adds the skepticism beat: 'Covering a language is not the same as sounding good in it... you still have to listen, language by language, before you trust it.' Coverage breadth, not verified per-lang quality.

hedged_or_kept.claim: Every 'beats the leader' TTS claim is a vendor blind test
hedged_or_kept.note: Manuscript states this explicitly as the skepticism beat (ch00-181 to ch00-183). Research confirms all 'beats ElevenLabs' numbers (Chatterbox 65.3%, Voxtral 68.4%, VoxCPM2 similarity) are vendor-run; VoxCPM2 reportedly loses the full benchmark.

hedged_or_kept.claim: Moonshine v2 beats Whisper on accuracy at a fraction of the size
hedged_or_kept.note: True per source (beats Whisper Large-v3 accuracy at far fewer params, built for Pi/phone). English-centric caveat from research omitted for fast-clip brevity; not a misstatement.

all_verified.claim: No new frontier open-weights model shipped in the window 2026-05-21 to 05-27
SGLang shipped a DeepSeek-V4 stability patch on 2026-05-26 (garbled decode on newest cards, crash under heavy load)
SGLang and vLLM are the two main open self-hosting engines
DeepSeek made its 75% V4-Pro price cut permanent ~2026-05-22; output ~$0.87 per 1M tokens, ~one quarter of launch
llama.cpp ships near-daily builds; in-window speed work on Vulkan, Intel, and phone-class chips
April Chinese open wave: DeepSeek V4, Qwen 3.6, Kimi K2.6 and more within ~2 weeks
Qwen 3.7 Max is API-only (no open weights); open Qwen still tops at 3.6; Mistral-style closed-flagship/open-mid-tier fork; no open Qwen 3.7 on Hugging Face as of the window
OpenRouter usage week May 18-24 (pub 05-26): DeepSeek V4-Flash #1 at ~3.43T tokens; Chinese models ~9.2T vs US ~4.9T; 4th straight week China leads usage
DeepSeek V4-Flash is open-weight, MIT-licensed, 284B total / 13B active MoE, 1M context
Tencent Hy3 surged on OpenRouter usage; Max Woolf teardown (2026-05-26): high cache-read cost makes effective price ~2x DeepSeek; spike likely one large app
Top of chat-quality and agent-terminal leaderboards is all closed models
Paper arguing benchmarks should be contamination-resistant submitted 2026-05-19
DeepSeek V4-Flash self-host needs ~170GB GPU memory; a pair of top data-center cards ~$7/hr cloud; API wins below very heavy traffic
Community quant groups (e.g. Unsloth) ship tuned/shrunk versions of new models within days
NVIDIA Parakeet is the speed pick for bulk server transcription
On 2026-05-21 Jensen Huang said Nvidia has largely conceded China's advanced-chip market to Huawei; China blocking even approved Nvidia imports
Chinese open models topping usage are increasingly trained/served on Huawei silicon; export controls bootstrapped a parallel open stack
Chatterbox (Resemble AI) is MIT-licensed, 23 languages, runs on-device; Chatterbox-Turbo (2026-03-26) uses a 1-step (vs 10-step) decoder for less compute
VoxCPM2 (OpenBMB) ~2B params, Apache 2.0, 30 languages, 48kHz, LoRA fine-tunable
MOSS-TTS-Nano ~100M params, runs on CPU with no GPU (single core on a MacBook), 20 languages
Mistral Voxtral TTS has open weights but a non-commercial (CC BY-NC 4.0) license; cannot ship in a paid product without a deal
Nearly every top open model is a mixture-of-experts (DeepSeek, Kimi, Qwen); total params = capacity, active params = per-token cost
